source: Spec 124 R-DA (McDonald's Airtight V3): every entry is the measured PRE -> POST diff of docs/reports/golden/classify_coa_trades/{pre,post}/{coa,standalone}.json. PRE = the legacy-shell captures of Night A-swap 2026-10-22 (lane COA-ASWAP); POST = the converted-shell captures retaken in the Fleet recapture night 2026-10-22 (run-20261022b; Spec 132 §x-captures.3 (R-DA); Q-B refresh from VALIDATE-REPORT-2 §2). Each why is explained from the descriptor deviation, register rule, runner code or the captures' own measured values it names, and states tonight's cause (the committed A-swap POSTs were empty-cursor runs; tonight's plain coa POSTs did real pending work because the coa root ran first). table_state[].content_hash moves for all three tables (coa_applications, lead_products, lead_trades) in both files; row counts 33,982 / 766,787 / 2,736,356 unchanged.

diffs.why: PIPELINE_META is derived from the descriptor outputs.writes (Spec 122 §5.1, R-BJ): the coa_applications write target lists [id, trade_classified_at] (key first); the legacy hand-written meta listed [trade_classified_at, id]. Same column set.

R-EQ shell swap: the legacy shell hand-printed JSON-log lines ("Loaded 35 trade configs / 805 logic variables from control panel", the classification progress and summary lines) and a hyphenated completion line; the runner prints its own lines (the target line "database=postgres user=postgres migrations=<n>", the ledger-gate line where the step gates, the PIPELINE_SUMMARY and PIPELINE_META lines and one "[classify_coa_trades] completed in <DUR>" line). Log lines only: no table, counter or verdict value is read from them, and the PIPELINE_SUMMARY content is diffed separately in the summary.* keys.
The runner titles the audit table with the descriptor identity.display_name "Classify CoA Trades"; the legacy literal was "CoA Trade Classification". The consumer reads rows, not the name.

audit_table.phase follows sharing.varies_by_chain.phase, the step's 1-based coa-chain index 7, generated by scripts/generate-sharing-phase.js (LCTP-D8 / the O1 fleet standard); the legacy literal was 42.
The library stamps every declared check row with observed before_write / after_write (FLEET-2 lib #52); the legacy hand-built rows had no such field.

The library stamps every declared check row with source "check" and every compute context row with source "context" (verdict.js checkRow / contextRow); the legacy hand-built rows carried no source field.

The converted table holds the declared checks only (coa_eligible, unmapped_scope_pct, avg_active_trades_per_lead, slug_resolution_miss_count, product_slug_miss_count, realtor_unavailable and the two vocab-coverage rows; Spec 132 §core.6), so rows shift against the legacy order and a status diff at an index compares two different metrics. coa_eligible (value_min 1, severity WARN, legacy :460-465, pinned L16) renders PASS on tonight's coa POST (2,329 processed) and WARN on the standalone POST (empty cursor), as the legacy PRE did (coa PASS on 2,334, standalone WARN). Verdict: coa PASS, standalone WARN in both shells.

The library renders the declared limit in force (e.g. "viol == 0", "pct <= 10") on each declared check row; the legacy rows carried the limit as prose or not at all. The bound is the step-owned variable in summary.records_meta.config.
